question: Sides AB and AC of ∆ ABC are produced to points D and E, respectively. The bisectors of ∠CBD and ∠BCE meet at P. If ∠A = 78°, then the measure of ∠P is:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] **__Shortcut Trick__**

Given, ∠A = 78°

If the bisectors of ∠CBD and ∠BCE meet at P

∠P = 90° - ∠A/2

⇒ ∠P = 90° - 78°/2

⇒ ∠P = 90° - 39° = 51°

∴ The measure of ∠P is 51°

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

∠A = 78°

Concept used:

The sum of all angles on a straight line is 180°

The sum of all angles of a triangle is 180°

**Calculation:**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/fbd7317490e6c0f169a91c3aeacefa1f839f36d07681ffd5aea11fa47596c9d5.png] 

∠ABC + ∠CBD = 180°

⇒ ∠CBD = 180° - ∠ABC

⇒ ∠CBD/2 = (180° - ∠ABC)/2

⇒ ∠CBP = 90° - ∠ABC/2 [∵ BP is the bisector of ∠CBD]

Similarly, ∠BCP = 90° - ∠ACB/2

In ΔBCP, ∠CBP + ∠BCP + ∠P = 180°

⇒ (90° - ∠ABC/2) + (90° - ∠ACB/2) + ∠P = 180°

⇒ 180° - (∠ABC + ∠ACB)/2 + ∠P = 180°

⇒ 180° - (180° - ∠BAC)/2 + ∠P = 180°

⇒ ∠P = (180° - ∠BAC)/2

⇒ ∠P = (180° - 78°)/2

⇒ ∠P = (102°)/2 = 51°

**∴ The measure of ∠P is 51°**
